A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GlobalConsistency and OmniTemp research. Their text, tables, equations, figures and appendices are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original temporal-relation extraction experiments, component ablations, annotation agreement and analyses of event distance and annotation consistency.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds MAVEN-ERE evaluation results and further numerical results with alternative LLMs.

M1.justification: Timeline prompting, DOT graph generation, five-generation aggregation and ILP consistency optimization are unchanged. Section 4.1 expands the batching explanation, while Appendix A retains the existing batching settings; this does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a restricted Wikipedia-domain TRE evaluation using MAVEN-ERE. The four existing news datasets remain. MAVEN-ERE's causal, coreference and subevent tasks are not evaluated, so this is a limited domain extension.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains RoBERTa, Bayesian, Bayesian + Constraints and Yuan et al.'s CoT baseline in the same comparisons. DeepSeek-V3 is another backbone for GlobalConsistency, not an added competing method. The new MAVEN-ERE experiment includes no external baseline.

E3.justification: The new MAVEN-ERE protocol selects validation documents with fewer than 200 pairs, evaluates BEFORE and SIMULTANEOUS relations, and uses the existing four-label prompt. DeepSeek-V3 adds a model configuration. Table 3 also revises its tokenization description to include DeepSeek's official tokenizer, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Component ablations, generation-count sensitivity, event-count and distance analyses, label inconsistency, and transitive-closure analysis are retained. The old Appendix F discussion is consolidated into Section 3.2 and appendix references, with Figure 11 preserved. The new tables provide additional benchmark and backbone scores.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 retains five-generation means and standard deviations for ZSL-Global and ZSL-Timeline, and single-run reporting for CoT and the ensemble methods. The uncertainty table moves from Table 5 to Table 7 with unchanged values; no new uncertainty estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Main results, costs and runtimes in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. v3 Table 5 adds DeepSeek-V3 scores of 55.1/74.4 on NT-6/OmniTemp and quantifies previously qualitative Llama/Gemini results. Table 6 adds MAVEN-ERE scores of 71.2 for GPT-4o and 64.9 for DeepSeek-R1. These are additional results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The label-distribution formulation, ILP objective, and uniqueness, symmetry and transitivity constraints are unchanged. The formal description moves from Appendix G to Appendix F; no mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the claims of global zero-shot graph generation, consistency optimization, OmniTemp's complete targeted-pair annotations and competitiveness with supervised models. The introduction reorganizes these contributions. Cross-domain applicability was already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly interprets the MAVEN-ERE results as confirming transferability beyond news. This adds a result-based applicability argument to v2's existing cross-domain motivation. The annotation-bias explanations, model-strength interpretation and stated limitations otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future OmniTemp release; v3 provides a repository stated to contain OmniTemp and all experimental code. Section 4.1 additionally specifies that every pair batch receives the full marked document and instructions. Existing hardware, training and optimizer details remain unchanged. Some future-release wording persists elsewhere.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al. (2022), the MAVEN-ERE dataset paper. Existing research positioning remains stable; the expanded CoT explanation reiterates a baseline already described as the strongest available zero-shot approach in v2.

P1.justification: v3 turns the introduction's contributions into bullets, expands baseline examples and batching explanations, adds acknowledgments, and divides Appendix B into model and dataset subsections. It also consolidates the transitive-closure discussion and renumbers appendices. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5–6 and gives Table 2 explicit non-exhaustive/exhaustive dataset groupings and revised highlighting. Several tables and figures move, and existing appendix tables are renumbered. All eleven figures retain the same underlying images.

improvement.justification: The restricted Wikipedia evaluation and explicit alternative-LLM scores modestly broaden and clarify empirical support. Concrete code/data access information and fuller batching documentation improve reproducibility information. These gains are limited by the new evaluation's two-relation scope and lack of baselines or uncertainty estimates, while inconsistent release-status wording remains. The principal method and evidence are unchanged.
